subject: Unit economics deep-dive: pricing & token volumes (follow-up)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechx.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-10T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: unit economics deep-dive 

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and the asks I promised to surface:

Call recap:
- Use case: real-time credit decision assistant in the FintechX mobile app (text + short context embeddings).
- Key features: 1) real-time suggestions (low latency), 2) monthly batch analytics (embeddings), 3) a small set of deterministic reranks.
- Current constraint: strict $/feature P&L target and CAC payback window (6–9 months).

Asks / info needed to run a first-pass unit economics model:
1) Expected token volumes: monthly prompts (avg tokens/request) and average responses. If you can give a low/likely/high range that would be ideal.
2) Target budget range for inference (monthly or $/1M tokens target).
3) Revenue per feature (or value metric) so we can model $/feature margin.
4) Typical customer acquisition cost (CAC) and desired payback window to compute payback months.

I ran an initial back-of-envelope example based on similar customers. High-level assumptions (please validate):
- 1M prompts/month -> 25M input tokens, 40M output tokens (~65M tokens total)
- Redwood baseline cost assumption (hosted) = $0.75 / 1M tokens for large chat models (example quantized variant)
- Inference cost -> $0.75 * 65 = $48.75 per month (this is illustrative, actual will vary with batching, cache, model choice)

But the metric you asked for — $/1M tokens — is easier to reason about. If your target is $X / 1M tokens, we can map that to $/feature by estimating tokens consumed per feature call and monthly usage.

I've attached an editable unit economics model (rwi_unit_econ_model.xlsx) with input fields for volumes, model mix, avg tokens per call, conversion and CAC. If you can drop your numbers into the sheet we’ll produce a $/feature and CAC-payback analysis.

Next steps I propose:
- You (or product ops) fill the volumes & revenue figures in the sheet
- Rishi and I will run two scenarios: conservative (no caching, lower batching) and optimized (prefix caching + batching + cheaper quantized model where acceptable)
- 30-minute follow-up next week to review outputs and confirm SLA/cost tradeoffs

Can you share the volumes and a realistic budget target (e.g., target $/1M tokens or monthly spend band)?

Cheers,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Follow-up: unit economics deep-dive 

Marissa — thanks for the recap and model. A few numbers from our side to help you run the scenarios: 

Volumes (monthly, low/likely/high):
- Prompts (unique user interactions): 200k / 350k / 600k
- Avg tokens per prompt: 40 / 60 / 80
- Avg tokens per response: 30 / 50 / 70
- Embedding requests (batch analytics): 1.2M / 2M / 3M embeddings (avg 512-d)

Budget: we are looking to keep inference spend under $10k/mo initially, and ideally target <$7k/mo if we can get good caching/batching. As a benchmark, the product team is thinking about a target of ~$120 / 1M tokens (this is internal target; curious how Redwood numbers map to this).

Revenue per feature: we estimate the credit-decision feature contributes on average $0.60 ARPU per active user per month (this is rough).

CAC: currently ~$45/customer; desired payback < 9 months.

I filled the sheet with the likely column — see attached. Happy to hop on the follow-up with Rishi & Marissa next Wed if that works.

—Alex
Product Lead, FintechX
alex.johnson@fintechx.com

Quoted original message:
> On Mon, Aug 10, 2026 at 3:05 PM, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> > Thanks again for taking the call today...

Attachments referenced: FintechX_filled_unit_econ.csv
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-11T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: unit economics deep-dive 

Alex — perfect, thanks for the numbers and for populating the sheet. A few quick notes before our scenario run: 

1) Your target of ~$120 / 1M tokens is significantly higher than our baseline hosted cost example — that baseline ($0.75 / 1M) I shared was for a very optimized, quantized runtime and was likely too low for your production latency SLO and model choice. For the models we discussed (low-latency chat + embeddings), a more realistic range for Redwood hosted is $50–$150 / 1M tokens depending on model size, quantization, caching, and contract commits.

2) With your likely volumes (350k prompts, avg 60/50 tokens), rough tokens/month ~ 350k*(60+50) = ~38.5M tokens (chat) plus embedding cost. Using a mid-range $80 / 1M tokens -> $3,080/mo inference cost (chat) + embeddings (we price embeddings per 1k or per embedding vector; I'll map your 2M embeddings to our embedding unit price in the model).

3) Translating to $/feature: if credit-decision is used by 200k DAUs with 1.5 events/user/month -> roughly (200k*1.5*tokens_per_call) map to per-month cost, then divide by active users or conversions to get $/feature. In your filled sheet I ran a quick calc: at mid-range pricing your $/feature ~ $0.02–$0.06 depending on model choice and caching. That compares to $0.60 ARPU, so margin on the feature can be healthy after CAC amortization if CAC payback < 9 months.

4) CAC payback: with $0.60 ARPU per user/month and inferred $/feature of $0.04, contribution margin per user ~ $0.56 before other product costs. At CAC $45 -> payback ~ 80 months if only this feature monetizes the user. But if your overall revenue per user is higher or multiple features are enabled, payback shortens. We usually model payback across the product suite and incremental ARPU attributable to the feature.

Next steps:
- Rishi & I will run the conservative and optimized runs using your likely numbers and return a short one-page summary (cost per 1M tokens mapping to $/feature and CAC-payback scenarios).
- Proposed follow-up: Wed Aug 18, 10:00–10:30am PT to review. Please let me know if that works.

Marking the model with the two scenario tabs — conservative / optimized.

Thanks,
Marissa

Alex / Marissa — jumping in with technical clarifications we’ll include in the two scenario runs: 

- Conservative: no prefix caching, minimal batching, standard float model (higher latency, higher cost). Embedding pricing at standard vector rate.
- Optimized: prefix/KV cache for repeated prompts, 2–3x effective token reduction for repeated flows, continuous batching during peak windows, and quantized LLM variant where latency SLO allows — expect 30–60% cost improvements depending on cache hit rate and model choice.

I’ll add an assumptions tab in the shared sheet with explicit per-unit inference rates we use so you can see how we translated $/1M tokens to per-call costs.

Also attaching the MAA draft (FintechX_MAA_v1.pdf) to show typical commercial terms for Dedicated vs Hosted pricing and commit tiers.

Will join the Wed slot if confirmed.
